titleEn: When the Window Lights Go Out, We Sleep Too!

pages.text: "This one is big, this one small." Riri in her yellow hat sorted shells into a box by size. Lights shone in the village windows outside. She puffed her cheeks, holding back a yawn. "Just finish this section!"
Mom peeped through the bedroom door. "Riri, bedtime." "I will sleep when they are all in! I am not sleepy." Riri kept her shell-filled hand over the box.
But yaaawn—yawns kept coming. Her hand stopped, then the box tipped over. Nine shells mixed together, and Riri began sorting again from the start.
Held in Mom's arms, Riri pressed her nose to the cold window glass. Lights shone in windows all over the village. "Riri, choose just one window." Riri pointed to the last house.
They watched that window quietly—and its light went out. "Oh! It is out!" Riri pressed her nose closer. Mom said softly, "That house has gone to sleep too."
The next window went dark, then the next. Riri slipped under the covers of the left bed. Mom kissed her forehead and sang, "When the window lights go out, we sleep too!"

Under the covers, Riri counted the remaining windows on her fingers. "Three... two... one." With each number, her eyelids grew heavier. "When the window lights go out, we sleep too!" she sang very softly.
Only one window was lit now—ours. "Mom, our house is last!" Riri whispered. Mom blew out the lamp by the window.

Riri pulled the covers to her chin and whispered, "One, count the window lights! Two, slip under the covers! Three, the last light is ours!" In the right bed, Lolo slept soundly with feet outside the covers.

Beneath the bright morning window, the shell box sat just as it had last night. Mom lifted Riri in both arms. "A good sleep makes morning come quickly, does it not?" "When the window lights go out, we sleep too!" Riri smiled.
